title: Coupling and Cohesion: Writing Loosely Coupled Code
summary: Quick revision notes on types of coupling, high cohesion, the Law of Demeter, composition over inheritance, dependency injection, and how SOLID and design patterns keep coupling low.

chapters.title: Coupling and Cohesion Mental Model
points: Coupling = how much one module must know about or change with another; cohesion = how closely a module's own parts belong together
Goal: low coupling between modules, high cohesion within a module; they reinforce each other
Test for coupling: if I change module A, how many other modules must change?
Test for cohesion: can you describe the module's job in one sentence without 'and'?
Low-cohesion smell: Utils, Manager or Helper classes that grow unrelated methods

chapters.title: Types of Coupling
points: Content coupling (worst): one module reads or modifies another's internals, such as direct access to private state or reflection hacks
Common coupling: modules share global mutable state, so any change can break any reader
Control coupling: caller passes a flag that steers the callee's logic (render(true)); fix with separate methods or polymorphism
Stamp coupling: passing a whole object when only one field is needed; fix by passing just the field or a narrow interface
Data coupling (best): modules share only the primitive arguments they need; message coupling (events, no knowledge of receiver) is even looser

chapters.title: High Cohesion and the Law of Demeter
points: Cohesion levels: functional (one well-defined task, best) > sequential > communicational > logical > coincidental (random grouping, worst)
Cohesion is the Single Responsibility Principle at module level: one reason to change
Law of Demeter: a method may call only on itself, its parameters, objects it creates, and its direct fields/collaborators
Violation smell: train-wreck chains like order.getCustomer().getAddress().getCity()
Fix by tell, don't ask: add order.shippingCity() that delegates; trade-off is more thin delegating methods, so don't wrap plain data structures or fluent builders

chapters.title: Composition over Inheritance and Dependency Injection
points: Inheritance is the tightest class coupling: the subclass depends on the parent's implementation (fragile base class problem)
Composition: hold a collaborator as a field and delegate to it; it is 'has-a', swappable at runtime, and testable with fakes
Use inheritance only for a true is-a with the Liskov guarantee; otherwise compose behind an interface
Dependency injection: a class receives its dependencies instead of constructing them (no new Mailer() inside the class)
Constructor injection is the default (immutable, dependencies explicit); setter injection for optional ones; avoid service locator and hidden globals

chapters.title: How SOLID and Patterns Serve Low Coupling
points: Dependency Inversion: high-level code depends on an abstraction it owns, and low-level details implement it
Open/Closed + Interface Segregation: extend via new implementations; small role interfaces avoid stamp coupling
Strategy and State replace conditionals and control-coupling flags with swappable objects; Factory hides concrete construction
Observer/Event bus gives message coupling: the publisher does not know subscribers; Facade and Adapter shield callers from subsystem details
Trade-off: too many interfaces and indirection (over-abstraction) hurts readability; add an abstraction only where change or testing demands it

chapters.title: Coupling and Cohesion Cheat Sheet
points: Coupling ladder worst to best: content, common, control, stamp, data, message
Cohesion ladder worst to best: coincidental, logical, communicational, sequential, functional
Demeter rule: talk to friends only; one dot per call is a good guide
Prefer composition + constructor injection; inheritance only for true is-a
Quick checks: does one change ripple? can I unit-test with a fake? does the class name need 'and'?
